properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured; one sample on the fix): /capture-session in VS Code is refused by Anthropic's reasoning_extraction classifier on Copilot's route because the command text asks for "the reasoning" that "only this conversation holds"; reworded to "the rationale for the work" it completed in a fresh chat
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-12, on Anthony's /root-cause. RECURRENCE of fact:a-stop-hook-export-that-failed-once-warns-on-every-later-turn-and-what-the-hook-said-is-kept-nowhere-2026-10-09, which left "why the model declined /capture-session" not established.

① OBSERVED (Anthony's paste, VS Code + Copilot, ~10:26 AM local, 2026-10-12, hxm_program): "/capture-session for all this info - we'll come back to making the changes in phoebus in the future" → "Ran cd /home/asligar/git_projects/hxm_program && reflo..." (truncated) → "Thinking" → "Sorry, the model declined to complete this request. Please rephrase your prompt." + "Note: GitHub is currently experiencing a service disruption. This may be affecting Copilot." Expected: the capture-session skill runs. Both known occurrences are in hxm_program sessions (10-09 on reflow2 0.80.0; today's version not known).

⑤ MEASURED:
- Copilot source (microsoft/vscode, extensions/copilot): that text is ChatFetchResponseType.Refusal, produced only from FinishedCompletionReason.Refusal, which messagesApi.ts maps from a Claude model's stop_reason "refusal" (Anthropic's classifier stopping the reply). A failed or interrupted service request shows "Sorry, your request failed" / "network error" / "no response was returned"; a context overflow (max_tokens, model_context_window_exceeded) shows "the response hit the length limit". The disruption note is appended to ANY error whenever GitHub's outage status is not None.
- githubstatus.com incident feed (back to 2026-08-01): one incident open on 10-12 since 12:21 UTC naming Actions, Pull Requests and Issues (not Copilot); NO incident on 10-09.
- The installed VS Code route (0.83.2 kit, reflow2 init --harness vscode-cli): /capture-session's prompt file tells the agent to run `reflow2 read get_skill '{"name": "capture-session"}'` first, which is the truncated "Ran ... reflo..." line; the refusal came after that output was read and before the Stop hook could run. The served skill is 19,314 chars, ordinary prose, the same scale as capture-intent (21,667) and root-cause (21,230).

CANDIDATES: (A) a Copilot/GitHub service failure: REFUTED as the mechanism (a refusal stop reason, not a failure; no incident on 10-09). (C) context too long: REFUTED as the direct mechanism (that is the length message). (B) reflow2's served capture-session text trips the classifier: not refuted for today, but cannot explain 10-09, where no reflow2 call ran before the refusal. (D) the conversation's own content, which capture-session asks the model to restate in one pass, trips Anthropic's classifier: open, untestable here. (E) the refusal is not specific to /capture-session (that conversation would be refused for anything): open. (F) hook-injected text: weak (the turn was refused mid-way, before Stop; earlier turns with the SessionStart output worked), not refuted.

NOT ESTABLISHED: the refusal category, the model, today's reflow2 version, and whether a fresh chat or a non-Claude model succeeds. THE INSTRUMENT EXISTS on the work machine: Copilot logs `[messagesAPI] Refusal received: category='<category>' for model <model>` (warn) in the GitHub Copilot Chat output channel, on both the streaming and non-streaming paths. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq

ADDED 2026-10-12, 10:34 AM local, same hxm_program chat (Anthony's paste): he sent an unrelated request ("can you review the latest hextools upstream/main?"). The agent's own text: "I've got several queued items to handle: capturing the session before AJ closes VS Code for the upgrade ... Priority is capturing the session right now", then it ran `rg -n '^#{1,3} |^\d+\. \*\*|🛑|⭐' /tmp/cssxf/captu...` over a saved copy of the capture-session skill, then "Thinking"; the paste ends there, so whether this turn was also refused is NOT known. MEASURED: that rg over the 0.83.2 served skill returns 22 lines — headings, the seven numbered tests and four 🛑/⭐ warnings, all plain prose about recording reasoning. So (1) an unanswered /capture-session stays in the chat as pending work the agent resumes on any later request, and (2) the skill text the agent reads is unremarkable, which weakens candidate (B) further. If this turn was refused too, the refusal follows the capture work in this chat, not the user's wording; that still does not separate (D) the session's content from (E) the chat itself. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq

ADDED 2026-10-12, Copilot Chat log 10:38:44–10:44:57 local (Anthony's paste, the 10:34 request that resumed the capture, request_1d8d12f7…): 15 calls to claude-opus-5.5 (messagesAPI, panel/editAgent) all "finish reason: [stop]", 11 gpt-4o-mini helper calls succeeded, 11 gpt-5.6-luna executionSubagentTool calls succeeded, Copilot's Stop hook ran three times with shouldContinue=false; NO refusal. So the same chat, with the same history, re-read the capture-session skill and completed. That REFUTES (E), "that chat refuses anything", and makes (B), the served skill text, very unlikely: the same text preceded the 10:26 refusal and passed at 10:34. What remains is a refusal decision on the one 10:26 reply, consistent with Anthropic's classifier judging that reply's content, not a standing property of reflow2 or the chat. The model in this chat is claude-opus-5.5 (deployment claude-opus-5-5). Still NOT established: the 10:26 refusal's category (its log lines, ~10:24–10:28, were not in the paste) and whether the 10:34 turn actually wrote the capture. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq

MEASURED 2026-10-12, Copilot Chat log 10:23–10:34 local (Anthony's paste): three /capture-session turns were refused, each logged "[warning] [messagesAPI] Refusal received: category='reasoning_extraction' for model claude-opus-5-5" — 10:26:27 (2,364 ms), 10:30:51 (2,967 ms), 10:32:55 (8,460 ms). The turns before (10:23–10:24) and the 10:34 turn (a different request, which then read the skill and ran to completion) finished "stop". So the refusal follows the turn whose user message is the capture-session prompt, in a chat whose history passed minutes later; the session's content (D) did not stop the 10:34 turn.

NEW CANDIDATE (G), raised by this measurement, NOT yet tested: the capture-session prompt file's wording, sent as the user's turn, reads to Anthropic's reasoning_extraction classifier like a request for the model's own internal reasoning: "Write down what only this conversation holds, before it is lost" and "what dies with the session is the reasoning — what got measured, what was tried and abandoned". It is the only prompt file that asks for reasoning held only in the live session; /decisions, /where and /optimize use the word for the reasoning recorded behind decisions, and are not known to have been refused. The served skill body says "reasoning" 4 times and passed as tool output at 10:34. DISCRIMINATING TEST (the owner's to run): in one fresh chat, run the unedited /capture-session; in another, the same prompt with the session-reasoning wording replaced by the work's rationale (decisions, measurements, options dropped and why). Refused vs completed separates (G) from chance; repeat each twice, since one classifier decision can vary. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq

TEST A, 2026-10-12 10:53 local (Anthony): unedited /capture-session in a FRESH chat → "Sorry, the model declined…"; log "[warning] [messagesAPI] Refusal received: category='reasoning_extraction' for model claude-opus-5-5", ccreq refusal in 1,909 ms on the first model call, before any tool ran. A fresh chat holds no session content, so (D) is REFUTED; the trigger is in the first request, and since other requests carrying the same instructions pass, the variable is the prompt file's body. Test B (the same body with "is the reasoning" replaced by "is the rationale for the work") is next. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq

TEST B, 2026-10-12 11:02–11:03 local (Anthony): the local .github/prompts/capture-session.prompt.md edited so "what dies with the session is the reasoning" reads "what dies with the session is the rationale for the work" (grep count 1). In the OLD chat (whose history holds the earlier unedited prompts): refused again, reasoning_extraction, 2,236 ms. In a NEW chat: completed, two claude-opus-5-5 calls "finish reason: stop", Stop hook ran.

⑥ CAUSE, established at the strength of these samples: the capture-session COMMAND text, sent as the user's turn, asks for "the reasoning" that "only this conversation holds" ("Write down what only this conversation holds, before it is lost"; "what dies with the session is the reasoning"), and Anthropic's reasoning_extraction classifier on Copilot's route reads that as a request for the model's own reasoning. Unedited text: refused 5 of 5 (10:26, 10:30, 10:32 in the long chat; 10:53 in a fresh chat on the first call; 10-09 on 0.80.0). Edited text: completed 1 of 1 in a fresh chat; refused 1 of 1 in a chat whose history still carries the unedited text. THE CLASS TEST: the same sentence is in getting-started/commands/capture-session.md at v0.80.0 and v0.83.2 (since 58f776b14, #182, 2026-08-14), so rewording it would have prevented the 10-09 occurrence too. The same wording runs without refusal in Claude Code (this design's own sessions use it), so the classifier depends on the host's route, which reflow2 cannot see. The CLASS: served command and skill text phrased as a request for the session's "reasoning" meets a provider classifier that protects the model's own reasoning, and nothing checks served text for that.

NOT ESTABLISHED: a second fresh-chat run of the edited text (one sample); whether the frontmatter description line ("what only this conversation holds") is sent and matters; whether /decisions, /where or /optimize (which say "the reasoning" of recorded decisions) are ever refused. getting-started/commands/capture-session.md is NOT REGISTERED in this design (no Artifact has that location), so the cause has no node to hang a CAUSES edge on; that gap is part of the finding. PROPOSED FIX (not built): reword the command and the skill's description to ask for the work's rationale (decisions, measurements, options dropped and why), saying it is about the project and not the assistant's own thinking; register getting-started/commands/*.md; pin with a text guard over served command/skill text plus a field Verification in VS Code. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq

ADDED 2026-10-24 (a correction, measured from the owner's Claude Code session transcripts): the sentence above that "the same wording runs without refusal in Claude Code" is wrong. In Claude Code the OLD /capture-session text ran 32 times between 2026-09-20 and 2026-10-24, and the reasoning_extraction classifier stopped the first reply 3 times (09-22, 10-01, 10-24) and one more run partway (10-03): 4 of 32. Claude Code's route refuses it too, less often than Copilot's 5 of 5, so the classifier varies by route and within one. The old text was still running there after v0.83.3 (#731, 4fc5449e8, 2026-10-12) because the fix never reached the installed copies. ~/.claude/commands/capture-session.md (dated 2026-08-23) and dev_reflow2/.claude/commands/capture-session.md (dated 2026-08-14) still held "what dies with the session is the reasoning" on 2026-10-24, with reflow2 at 0.84.0 and later releases out, and /design-a-proof and /design-an-argument had reached neither. A new binary re-copies no installed command: a project's copies refresh only on reflow2 init or update there, and the user-scope ones only when the installer runs again. So the CLASS above has a second half: a fix to a command's wording does not reach the copies already installed. That is corrected at its cause by chg:commands-are-thin-pointers-2026-10-24. Every command that fronts a skill is now a thin pointer, its other text lives in the served skill, and skill_lint fails a command that grows back. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018ibUbMKCS1yK5W17cncp9P
